newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador lawmakers oust Bucaram, name new president.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador lawmakers oust Bucaram, name new president.

text.p: Ecuador's Congress voted by a narrow majority on Thursday to oust embattled President Abdala Bucaram, a quirky populist who took office just six months ago, on grounds of mental incompetence.
The move, which Bucaram called "unconstitutional," was passed by a 44-34 majority and Congress immediately moved to swear in its leader, Fabian Alarcon, as the country's new president.

The ousting of Bucaram, who took office promising to be the president of Ecuador's vast majority of poor, came just one day after the country was virtually shut down by a massive nationwide strike to protest harsh economic austerity measures the government clamped on the nation in early January.

The measures, which drove Bucaram's approval rating down almost as quickly as the cost of living shot up, included electricity and gas rate hikes totaling more than 200 percent and a 60 percent rise in bus fares.

Car horns in downtown Quito blared in celebration of Bucaram's deposal as Alarcon, who was accused by Vice President Rosalia Arteaga Wednesday of engineering a congressional coup, was sworn in as acting president.
Alarcon is to hand over to a new, popularly elected head of state in August 1998.
